description: Enroll a whole audience (everyone, lists, a segment, a filter, or combined rules) into a sequence as a background run. Unlike enroll_subscribers_in_sequence there is no 500-contact cap: the worker walks the audience in batches, skips contacts already in the sequence (and, for one_time sequences, anyone who completed or was cancelled before), never enrolls unsubscribed or bounced contacts, and reports progress. This is how a manual-trigger countdown sequence (Black Friday) gets its audience: enable the sequence, then call this. Late enrollees skip the steps whose key date already passed. Pass data for run-level values that are the same for everyone in the run (a sale end time, a discount percentage); the sequence's emails read them as {{enrollment.FIELD}}. Defaults to dryRun, which only returns the estimate (matchingCount, alreadyEnrolledCount, enrollableCount); pass dryRun false to start the run and poll get_sequence_audience_enrollment. One run per sequence at a time.

audience.description: Who to enroll. { type: 'all' } for every active contact with an email, { type: 'lists', listIds: [...] }, { type: 'segment', segmentId: '...' }, { type: 'filtered', filters: [...] } with subscriber filters, or { type: 'rules', include: [...], exclude: [...] } combining several. For hand-picked contacts beyond the 500 cap of enroll_subscribers_in_sequence, use { type: 'rules', include: [], includedSubscriberIds: [...] }. Same shape as campaign targetLists.

excludedCampaignOpenerIds.description: Exclude contacts who opened any of these campaigns.

excludedSubscriberIds.description: Contacts removed from the include rules. Does not remove includedSubscriberIds.

includedSubscriberIds.description: Specific contacts to enroll in addition to the include rules. Unsubscribed, bounced and email-less contacts are skipped.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

data.description: Optional run-level data (with dryRun false): a JSON object of values shared by everyone in this run, up to 8 KB, for example {"sale_ends_at": "2026-11-29T23:59:00Z", "discount_percent": 20}. Each enrolled contact keeps a copy; emails and conditions in the sequence read it as {{enrollment.sale_ends_at}}. Returned as data on the run. Auto-enroll syncs do not carry run data.

dryRun.description: Defaults to true: estimate only. Pass false to start enrolling.

scheduledFor.description: ISO 8601 date-time to start the run later instead of now (with dryRun false). The run stays queued until then and can be cancelled before it starts.

sequenceId.description: Sequence ID to enroll the audience in.

targetNodeId.description: Optional node ID to start contacts at. Defaults to the first step after the trigger.

name: enroll_sequence_audience

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `enroll_sequence_audience` MCP tool.

alreadyEnrolledCount.description: Estimate only: matching contacts skipped because they are already in the sequence.

audienceEnrollment.description: Started run: id, status, estimatedCount, processedCount, enrolledCount, skippedCount, targetNodeId, data (run-level values read as {{enrollment.*}}, or null) and timestamps. Null for estimates. includedSubscriberCount gives the number of hand-picked contacts; audience.includedSubscriberIds lists at most the first 20, with includedSubscriberIdsTruncated true when cut.

dryRun.description: True when this call only estimated the audience instead of starting a run.

enrollableCount.description: Estimate only: contacts that would be enrolled.

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

matchingCount.description: Estimate only: contacts matching the audience.

message.description: Human-readable status, confirmation, or next-step message.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
